content:
[0] AI data centers are being built at massive scale in the US, which has heavily impacted the entire consumer electronics industry. Huge bulk orders of high-end HBM2 DRAM have completely reshaped supply chains, making it extremely difficult to obtain consumer-grade memory and storage products.

[1] This year, the prices of SSD and DDR5 RAM have skyrocketed. Apple finally adjusted its pricing at the end of June — raising prices across the entire lineup by between $100 and over $400. Even with the price hikes, the company still struggles to keep the MacBook Air in stock.

[2] In June, Apple raised the price of the MacBook Air from $1,099 to $1,299. Earlier, when the M5 model launched in March, it had already seen a small increase from $999 to $1,099. Of course, Apple also doubled the base storage configuration from 256GB to 512GB, so for users who already needed more storage, it actually represents a real gain.

[3] However, even with price hikes to offset rising memory and storage costs, Apple still struggles to keep the M5 MacBook Air in stock — even though this computer is fairly new.

[4] According to Mark Gurman, if you order a MacBook Air from Apple right now, it will take until at least the end of this month to arrive, and retail channels are describing MacBook Air supply as 'the tightest they can remember.'

[5] Apple's recent 'Back to School' promotion also specifically notes that MacBook Air availability depends on stock — an extremely unusual situation for a product that is in the middle of its product cycle.

[6] The reason behind the MacBook Air supply shortage

[7] According to Gurman's sources, this shortage is due to the memory crisis, but it also involves Apple prioritizing production for the base model M5 MacBook Pro in preparation for an update this fall. From the 'Power On' newsletter:

[8] As far as I know, the MacBook Air shortage is indeed related to the ongoing memory crunch. Apple has been trying to ease the problem by preparing to source memory from Chinese suppliers, at least for products sold in China.

[9] Overall, the next few years will be a difficult period for Apple. The company has warned that next quarter's sales will be affected by supply constraints and has also warned that further price hikes are possible. We may see more Mac products adjust their prices to balance demand.

[10] Amazon currently has the M5 MacBook Air in stock with next-day delivery and a $100 discount. If you've been considering buying one, this may be your last chance before the situation at third-party channels worsens.
